# Date Versioning (DateVer)

> A versioning standard in which a version number is the date it was released: YY.MM.DD, with -1, -2 and so on for further releases on the same day. Created and maintained by Stux.Group. Current specification: {{spec_version}}.

The essentials (the specification is the source of truth):

- Format: YY.MM.DD, each part two digits and zero-padded, a real calendar date. Example: 26.10.01.
- The date is the UTC date of the release.
- Further releases on the same UTC date append -N, counting from 1 with no gaps: 26.10.01-1, 26.10.01-2. Never -0.
- Precedence: compare YY, MM, DD, then N numerically (no suffix means N = 0), so 26.10.01 < 26.10.01-1 < 26.10.02. Later versions always rank higher.
- Never compare a Date Version with SemVer rules: in SemVer 26.10.1-1 ranks before 26.10.1, but in DateVer 26.10.01-1 ranks after 26.10.01.
- SemVer form, for registries that only accept SemVer: MAJOR = YY without leading zeros, MINOR = MM without leading zeros, PATCH = DD x 100 + N. Example: 26.10.01-2 becomes 26.10.102, 05.03.09-4 becomes 5.3.904. A project whose old SemVer versions would outrank that form (major already 26 or more) adds a fixed major offset, the smallest multiple of 100 that fixes it: 26.10.01 becomes 126.10.100.
- Switching from another scheme: say so in the first Date Version's changelog entry; every Date Version ranks above every version from before the switch.
- Optional build metadata after a plus sign (+build.7) is ignored for precedence. A leading v is only for tag names (v26.10.01).
